moved.sentence: To be installable an app **MUST** be served over HTTPS (or `localhost` in development) and **MUST** link a valid Web App Manifest.

judged.note: Both MUSTs are kept, one per rule, each with the 'to be installable' scope; the localhost-in-development exception is kept.
The 'MUST include, at minimum' lead-in is carried at MUST by the three manifest rules (core fields, 192/512 icons, id).
Kept at MUST with name (or short_name), start_url, and all three allowed display values.

moved.sentence: `icons` with both a 192x192 and a 512x512 entry.

judged.note: Kept at MUST with both the 192x192 and the 512x512 entry.

moved.sentence: Include a `maskable` icon for adaptive shaping.

judged.note: The unkeyed instruction is kept at SHOULD with its reason (adaptive shaping). The baseline list makes only 192x192 and 512x512 required, so SHOULD matches the old sentence's level.

moved.sentence: `id` to give the install a stable identity across `start_url` changes.

judged.note: The manifest id is kept at MUST with its reason (stable identity across start_url changes).

moved.sentence: Validate against Lighthouse / DevTools Application panel before shipping; do not hand-assert installability.

judged.note: Validating with Lighthouse / DevTools before shipping is kept at SHOULD, and 'do not hand-assert installability' at SHOULD NOT.

moved.sentence: An installable app SHOULD ship a Web App Manifest and a service worker with an explicit caching strategy, and MUST account for iOS/Safari limitations.

judged.note: Both clauses are kept at their levels: the SHOULD for manifest plus service worker with an explicit caching strategy, and the MUST for iOS/Safari limitations, each scoped to installable apps.

moved.sentence: If installability is not a requirement, do not add a service worker for its own sake (YAGNI).

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD NOT with the 'installability is not a requirement' condition and the YAGNI reason.

moved.sentence: As of iOS 18 / Safari 18 the following hold; re-verify per release:

judged.note: The as-of date (iOS 18 / Safari 18) and the re-verify-per-release instruction are kept at SHOULD for the iOS/Safari constraints.

moved.sentence: **Background Sync / Periodic Background Sync are unavailable.** Do not depend on them; queue writes in IndexedDB and flush on next foreground.

judged.note: The fact (Background Sync / Periodic Background Sync unavailable) is kept in the iOS constraints rationale part; 'do not depend on them' is kept at SHOULD NOT; queue-in-IndexedDB-and-flush-on-foreground is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Treat all client storage as a cache, never as the source of truth.

judged.note: Kept, strengthened to MUST: all client storage is a cache, never the source of truth.

moved.sentence: Web Push availability has been subject to EU regulatory variation (iOS 17.4+); confirm behavior in target regions rather than assuming uniform support. (FORECAST: regional policy continues to evolve.)

judged.note: The EU regulatory variation (iOS 17.4+) and the confirm-in-target-regions instruction are kept at SHOULD; the FORECAST note is kept in the iOS constraints rationale part.

moved.sentence: Register the service worker after the page loads and choose a caching strategy per request class — **do not** apply one strategy globally:

judged.note: Registering after page load is kept at SHOULD; choosing per request class is kept at SHOULD with the 'do not apply one strategy globally' prohibition.

moved.sentence: Precache the app shell so navigations resolve offline.

judged.note: Precaching the app shell is kept at SHOULD with its reason (navigations resolve offline).

moved.sentence: Prefer a maintained library (Workbox) over hand-rolled fetch handlers unless the surface is trivial — this is a deliberate trade for correctness on edge cases (range requests, opaque responses), not a mandate.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the Workbox example, the trivial-surface exception and the full reason (edge-case correctness, not a mandate).
